common_name: Kashi Pragati Okra (IIVR Disease-Resistant Indian Bhindi)

planting.note: Direct sow once soil is thoroughly warm; this IIVR release begins flowering around five weeks after sowing and can be resown for a second rainy-season crop in warm climates.

directions: Released by ICAR's Indian Institute of Vegetable Research in Varanasi, Kashi Pragati is a tall, open-pollinated okra bred for dual resistance to yellow vein mosaic virus and okra leaf curl virus, two begomovirus diseases that routinely cripple susceptible plantings across the Indian plains. Plants begin flowering about 36-38 days after sowing and carry roughly two dozen pods per plant, so frequent picking at the tender 8-10 cm stage keeps quality high and encourages continued set. It has become one of the most widely adapted okra releases from the ICAR system, recommended across a broad swath of states from Punjab to Odisha, and performs well in both the rainy kharif season and the hotter summer crop. Grow it in full sun on fertile, well-drained soil with steady moisture through flowering and pod fill.
sources: ICAR-Indian Institute of Vegetable Research (IIVR), Varanasi — Okra Varieties
BioVoiceNews — Kashi Pragati variety impact report

planting.note: Direct sow into warm soil; this IIHR release carries virus resistance bred in from a wild relative, so it tolerates heavier regional disease pressure than ordinary okra lines.

directions: Arka Anamika was bred at the Indian Institute of Horticultural Research in Bangalore by crossing cultivated okra (IIHR 20-31) with a wild relative, Abelmoschus manihot subsp. tetraphyllus, then backcrossing to recover a productive okra type while keeping resistance to yellow vein mosaic virus, a disease that otherwise devastates susceptible crops in warm, humid regions. Plants grow tall and well-branched with a purple cast to the green stems, bearing spineless, five-to-six-ridged pods with a notably delicate aroma and good cooking and keeping quality. Fruiting comes in two flushes, first along the main stem around 45-50 days after sowing and later on side branches, giving an extended harvest window over its roughly 130-day cropping cycle. Grow it in full sun on fertile, well-drained soil with consistent moisture, picking pods young and often to sustain the second flush.
sources: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bangalore — Okra Arka Anamika variety profile
National Horticulture Board (India)

common_name: Kashi Urvasi Bitter Gourd (IIVR Long Dark-Green Karela)

planting.note: Direct sow after soil has fully warmed and provide a trellis; this IIVR release suits both the summer and rainy-season bitter gourd crops common across northern India.

directions: Kashi Urvasi was developed at ICAR's Indian Institute of Vegetable Research in Varanasi from the cross IC-85650B x IC-44435A and has since been notified for cultivation in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, and Jharkhand by the UP State Horticultural Seed Sub-Committee. Vines bear long, dark green fruit with mild surface projections, typically 16-18 cm and 90-110 g, reaching first picking stage 55-60 days after sowing with reported field yields of 20-22 t/ha. Fruits hold their color and firmness well after harvest, making the variety popular with both home gardeners and market growers for classic karela preparations. Give plants a sturdy trellis, full sun, and generous, even moisture, since bitter gourd vines are shallow-rooted and quick to stress in dry soil.
sources: ICAR-Indian Institute of Vegetable Research (IIVR), Varanasi — Bitter Gourd Varieties
Indian Horticulture journal (ICAR ePubs)

common_name: Arka Lohit Chilli (IIHR High-Pungency Indian Hot Pepper)

planting.note: Start indoors about 8 weeks before last frost and transplant once nights stay warm; this tall IIHR release suits both irrigated and rainfed chile plantings.

directions: Arka Lohit is a pure-line selection made by the Indian Institute of Horticultural Research in Bangalore from a local Karnataka collection known as IHR 324. Plants grow tall and upright, carrying smooth, firm, pendant fruits about 7-8 cm long that mature from dark green to red and rank among the more pungent Indian chile releases, with measured capsaicin content near 0.7%. It is grown for both the fresh green market and the dried red chile trade, with reported yields around 25 t/ha green or 3 t/ha dried over a roughly 180-day crop cycle, and is recommended across a wide band of states from Chhattisgarh and Odisha to Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Grow in full sun on well-drained soil; it tolerates both irrigated beds and rainfed conditions once established.
sources: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bangalore — Chilli Arka Lohit variety profile
National Horticulture Board (India)

common_name: Kashi Early Chilli (IIVR F1 Hybrid Early Green Chile)

planting.note: Start indoors 8 weeks before last frost; this IIVR F1 hybrid was bred for an earlier, concentrated harvest than standard open-pollinated chile lines.

directions: Kashi Early is an F1 hybrid chile bred at ICAR's Indian Institute of Vegetable Research in Varanasi by crossing the lines PBC-473 and KA-2. Plants grow 100-110 cm tall with dull green, unpigmented stems and bear long, attractive, dark green pendant fruits about 8-9 cm long, held for an earlier and more uniform harvest window than many traditional Indian chile varieties. It was developed primarily for growers in Uttar Pradesh seeking a dependable early hybrid for the fresh green chile market. Grow it in full sun on fertile, well-drained soil with steady moisture, and expect first harvest noticeably sooner after transplanting than open-pollinated chile types.
sources: ICAR-Indian Institute of Vegetable Research (IIVR), Varanasi — Chilli Varieties
Krishak Jagat — IIVR chilli hybrid variety report

common_name: KAT B1 Bean (Kenyan Heat-Tolerant Yellow Bush Bean)

planting.note: Sow after soil has warmed, mirroring the onset of Kenya's short rains in low to mid-altitude semi-arid plantings.

directions: KAT B1 is a compact, determinate bush bean bred at KALRO's Katumani dryland research station to give farmers in hot, low-to-mid altitude semi-arid Kenya a reliable crop despite erratic rainfall. Known locally as Kathika or Soya Njano, it flowers quickly with light pink blossoms and reaches harvest in about 60-65 days, letting it escape terminal drought that would damage slower-maturing beans. The round, greenish-yellow seed cooks to a sweet flavor with less flatulence than many local bean types, and the plant carries broad field tolerance to rust and common bean mosaic virus. Grow in full sun with light, well-drained soil and modest irrigation during pod fill for best yield.
sources: Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Organization (KALRO) Katumani common bean variety release information
Pan-Africa Bean Research Alliance (PABRA) Kenya bean variety guides

common_name: KAT B9 Bean (Kenyan Dark Red Dryland Bush Bean)

planting.note: Direct sow as soil warms to match Kenya's short, unreliable rainfall windows in semi-arid growing areas.

directions: KAT B9, known locally as Gacuma, is an early-maturing bush bean released by KALRO's Katumani research station for Kenya's drier lowland growing areas with short or unpredictable rains. It produces dark red, long oblong seeds and flowers uniformly around 30-40 days after sowing, giving a concentrated pod-fill window that simplifies a single harvest pass. The variety carries field resistance to bean rust and is often cooked together with maize, where its red seed coat lends a characteristic brown color to the dish. Plant in full sun on well-drained soil and avoid waterlogging, since this variety is bred primarily for drought escape rather than wet conditions.
sources: Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Organization (KALRO) Katumani common bean variety release information
Pan-Africa Bean Research Alliance (PABRA) Kenya bean variety guides

common_name: H6213 Maize (Kenyan Late-Maturing Highland Hybrid Corn)

planting.note: Needs a long, reliably rainy season, so it is sown with the onset of the main long-rains planting window in Kenya's high-potential highland zones.

directions: H6213 is Kenya Seed Company's flagship late-maturing hybrid maize, bred for the country's high-potential highland growing zones above roughly 1,500 meters elevation where rainfall is abundant and well distributed. Because the hybrid needs a full 160-210 day season with at least 800mm of rain, it is suited to long-rains plantings in places like the Rift Valley highlands and western Kenya rather than lowland or short-season fields. Plants grow tall with strong standability and useful field tolerance to lodging, grey leaf spot, and ear rot, and the grain is valued by millers for good flour quality. Grow in full sun with consistent soil moisture through the long growing season to reach the variety's full yield potential.
sources: Kenya Seed Company Ltd. H6213 hybrid maize variety information
Kenya highland maize variety extension guides

common_name: Nyota Bean (Kenyan Iron-Rich Red Mottled Bush Bean)

planting.note: Direct sow once soil has warmed, timed to low-to-medium rainfall growing seasons in its recommended altitude band.

directions: Nyota, meaning 'star' in Swahili, is a biofortified common bean developed by KALRO with support from PABRA and AGRA to raise dietary iron and zinc intake among Kenyan smallholder households. It carries a distinctive brilliant red-mottled seed coat, flowers with light pink blossoms around 30-40 days after sowing, and reaches harvest in roughly 60-70 days with an unusually uniform, even pod-fill that supports a single clean harvest. The variety is recommended for low-to-medium altitude zones of about 1,000-1,600 meters under modest annual rainfall, and it is also popular with cooks for needing noticeably less cooking time than many older local bean types. Grow in full sun on well-drained soil with light watering through flowering and pod set.
sources: Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Organization (KALRO) common bean variety release information
Pan-Africa Bean Research Alliance (PABRA) biofortified bean program reports

common_name: KARI Mtama 1 Sorghum (Kenyan White Grain Sorghum)

planting.note: Direct sow into warm soil once seasonal rains are established across its wide elevation range.

directions: KARI Mtama 1 is an open-pollinated white grain sorghum released in 2000 by Kenya's then-KARI (now KALRO) for a wide elevation range from lowland areas up to about 1,800 meters, including cooler highland margins where the better-known Gadam sorghum does not perform well. It is a tall-growing type bearing large, cream-white grain heads and shows useful field tolerance to head smut and stem borer. Its malt characteristics are close enough to barley that Kenyan breweries use the grain for lager-style beer production alongside traditional flour and porridge uses. Direct sow into warm soil after rains are established, guard ripening heads against birds, and let them dry fully before threshing.
sources: Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Organization (KALRO) / KARI sorghum variety release records
East African Breweries Limited sorghum farming guides

planting.note: Sow or transplant after soil has warmed; regular leaf picking begins roughly 10-14 weeks after planting.

directions: SS49, released under the name 'Olevolosi', is a broad-leaved African nightshade selection bred from regional Solanum scabrum germplasm by AVRDC (the World Vegetable Center) at its Arusha, Tanzania station beginning around 2011, and subsequently registered and distributed to growers across East Africa including Kenya. It is distinguished from generic local managu landraces by notably wide, tender leaves and purple-petaled flowers that develop into purple berries. Plants begin flowering around 75 days after sowing, but growers typically start cutting leaves for the pot-herb market at 10-14 weeks and can continue harvesting over several pickings if the plants are kept from fully bolting. Grow in fertile, moisture-retentive soil in full sun to light shade and pick young leaves regularly to encourage continued vegetative regrowth.
sources: AVRDC — The World Vegetable Center African nightshade variety release records
KALRO Katumani Research Centre indigenous vegetable seed program
